title: Fulfillments
description: Track shipments and delivery of product orders.

help.title: About Fulfillments
help.overview: A fulfillment is one shipment of a product order: which order lines and how many units left, with which carrier and tracking. Shipping an order creates one automatically; you can also create one here to split an order into several parcels. Its status — pending, shipped, delivered, or failed — drives the order's shipped and delivered status.

sections.title: Creating a shipment
sections.body: A shipment can only cover what is still unshipped.
items: Pick the order, then the lines and the quantity of each. Every line must belong to that order, and the quantity cannot exceed what earlier shipments left open.
A shipment created here starts as pending: nothing has left yet and stock is untouched.
Once created, the order and the lines are fixed. Carrier, tracking, dates, and notes stay editable.

sections.title: How a shipment moves
sections.body: Ship, deliver, and fail are actions, each legal only from the status named here. They need permission to write the shipment status.
items: Ship is only from pending, and only when the order is not pending, cancelled, or refunded. It records the shipped time and the tracking you enter.

Shipping takes the units out of stock: the order's holds are consumed in the warehouses they were reserved in. Units that were never held are reserved on the spot; if there is not enough stock, the shipment is refused as out of stock.
Deliver is only from shipped. When the last shipment that did not fail is delivered, the order becomes delivered and the customer is told once.

Fail is from pending or shipped. Failing a parcel that already left puts its units back on hand and holds them for the order again, so a new shipment can take them. If the order is cancelled or refunded by then, those units are released instead.

sections.title: What the order sees
sections.body: The order's fulfillment status is computed from its shipments every time one changes.
items: Every line fully shipped makes the order fulfilled; some lines shipped make it partially fulfilled.
All lines shipped moves the order to shipped. A fully shipped order whose shipment failed goes back to processing.
Each change adds an entry to the order timeline.

sections.title: What you record on it
sections.body: The shipment, not the order, is where tracking lives.
items: Carrier, tracking number, and tracking link are what the customer receives in the shipping message.
Estimated delivery, shipped at, and delivered at mark the timeline. Notes are for staff.
Each line shows the product it ships, with its title and image.

sections.title: Related pages
items: Open the order for payment, cancel, or refund; those stay on the order.
A received return request puts goods back in the warehouse the line shipped from.
Deleting a shipment is a soft delete and it can be restored.
